chapter1.title: Chapter 1:Historical Development and Classification of Computers
chapter1.description: This chapter covers the historical development and classification of computers.

questions.question: Who is known as the Father of the Computer?
questions.explanation: Charles Babbage designed the Difference Engine and Analytical Engine.

questions.question: Why is Charles Babbage called the Father of the Computer?
questions.answerText: Because he designed the Difference Engine and Analytical Engine which formed the basis of modern computers.
questions.explanation: His designs introduced the idea of programmable computers.

questions.question: Who is regarded as the first computer programmer?
questions.explanation: Ada Lovelace wrote algorithms for Babbage's Analytical Engine.

questions.question: State the contribution of Augusta Ada Byron (Ada Lovelace).
questions.answerText: She wrote the first algorithm and is regarded as the first computer programmer.
questions.explanation: She worked with Charles Babbage's Analytical Engine.

questions.question: Which device was invented by Blaise Pascal?
questions.explanation: Pascal invented the Pascaline in 1642.

questions.question: John Napier invented ______.
questions.explanation: Napier's Bones was an early calculating device.

questions.question: Briefly explain Napier's Bones.
questions.answerText: A calculating device invented by John Napier for multiplication and division.
questions.explanation: It simplified arithmetic calculations.

questions.question: Who invented the Arithmometer?
questions.explanation: Thomas de Colmar developed the first commercially successful calculator.

questions.question: Herman Hollerith is remembered for inventing the ______ machine.
questions.explanation: His punched-card system was used for census processing.

questions.question: State the contribution of Herman Hollerith.
questions.answerText: He invented the punched-card tabulating machine used for data processing.
questions.explanation: His work influenced modern data processing systems.

questions.question: ENIAC stands for ______.
questions.explanation: ENIAC was one of the earliest electronic computers.

questions.question: Who developed ENIAC?
questions.answerText: John Mauchly and Presper Eckert.
questions.explanation: They jointly designed and built ENIAC.

questions.question: Which machine is considered the first general-purpose electronic computer?
questions.explanation: ENIAC was a major breakthrough in computing.

questions.question: What is the Abacus?
questions.answerText: An ancient calculating device consisting of beads moved on rods.
questions.explanation: It is one of the earliest calculating tools.

questions.question: The Analytical Engine introduced the concept of a programmable computer.
questions.explanation: It contained input, processing and output features.

questions.question: Briefly explain the Analytical Engine.
questions.answerText: A mechanical computer designed by Charles Babbage that could perform general calculations using stored instructions.
questions.explanation: It is regarded as the prototype of modern computers.

questions.question: Which machine was designed specifically to calculate mathematical tables?
questions.explanation: The Difference Engine automated mathematical calculations.

questions.question: Briefly explain the Difference Engine.
questions.answerText: A mechanical calculating machine designed by Charles Babbage for generating mathematical tables.
questions.explanation: It reduced human calculation errors.

questions.question: The Slide Rule was mainly used for ______.
questions.explanation: The Slide Rule was widely used before electronic calculators.

questions.question: State one contribution of John Napier to computing history.
questions.answerText: He invented Napier's Bones and introduced logarithms.
questions.explanation: His work simplified arithmetic operations.

questions.question: Computer hardware refers to the ______ components of a computer system.
questions.explanation: Hardware consists of the physical parts that can be seen and touched.

questions.question: Define computer hardware.
questions.answerText: Computer hardware refers to the physical components of a computer system that can be seen and touched.
questions.explanation: Examples include monitor, keyboard, CPU and printer.

questions.question: Computer software consists of programs and instructions used by a computer.
questions.explanation: Software enables the hardware to perform useful tasks.

questions.question: Define computer software.
questions.answerText: Computer software is a collection of programs, procedures and instructions that direct computer operations.
questions.explanation: Software tells hardware what to do.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a hardware component?
questions.explanation: Microsoft Word is application software.

questions.question: The four major components of computer hardware are ______.
questions.explanation: These are the basic functional units of a computer.

questions.question: Mention the four major components of computer hardware.
questions.answerText: Input Unit, Processing Unit, Storage Unit and Output Unit.
questions.explanation: Every computer system contains these functional units.

questions.question: Which hardware component is regarded as the brain of the computer?
questions.explanation: The CPU performs processing and control functions.

questions.question: Give two examples of input devices.
questions.answerText: Keyboard and Mouse.
questions.explanation: Input devices are used to enter data into the computer.

questions.question: Which of the following is an output device?
questions.explanation: Output devices display processed information.

questions.question: RAM stands for ______.
questions.explanation: RAM is the main temporary memory of a computer.

questions.question: ROM stands for ______.
questions.explanation: ROM stores permanent instructions.

questions.question: State one difference between RAM and ROM.
questions.answerText: RAM is volatile while ROM is non-volatile.
questions.explanation: RAM loses data when power is off; ROM does not.

questions.question: RAM loses its contents when power is switched off.
questions.explanation: RAM is volatile memory.

questions.question: Which memory is non-volatile?
questions.explanation: ROM retains data permanently.

questions.question: Mention three differences between RAM and ROM.
questions.answerText: RAM is volatile while ROM is non-volatile; RAM is read/write while ROM is mainly read-only; RAM stores temporary data while ROM stores permanent instructions.
questions.explanation: These are common examination differences.

questions.question: Primary memory is directly accessible by the CPU.
questions.explanation: Primary memory works closely with the processor.

questions.question: Give two examples of primary memory.
questions.answerText: RAM and ROM.
questions.explanation: These memories are directly connected to the CPU.

questions.question: Which of the following is secondary storage?
questions.explanation: Hard disks provide long-term data storage.

questions.question: State one difference between primary and secondary memory.
questions.answerText: Primary memory is directly accessible by the CPU while secondary memory is not.
questions.explanation: Secondary memory stores data permanently.

questions.question: Hard disk storage belongs to which technology?
questions.explanation: Hard disks use magnetic storage technology.

questions.question: Flash drives belong to ______ storage technology.
questions.explanation: Flash drives use semiconductor memory chips.

questions.question: CD-ROM and DVD are examples of ______ storage.
questions.explanation: Optical storage uses laser technology.

questions.question: Give one example of paper storage.
questions.answerText: Punch card or paper tape.
questions.explanation: Paper storage was used in early computing.

questions.question: Mention the four storage technologies.
questions.answerText: Semiconductor, Magnetic, Optical and Paper Storage.
questions.explanation: Storage devices are classified into these technologies.

questions.question: A USB flash drive is an example of ______ storage.
questions.explanation: It stores data electronically in memory chips.

questions.question: What is a computer port?
questions.answerText: A port is an interface used to connect external devices to a computer.
questions.explanation: Ports enable communication between devices.

questions.question: Which port is commonly used for flash drives?
questions.explanation: USB ports connect flash drives and many peripherals.

questions.question: Which connector is commonly used to connect a monitor?
questions.explanation: VGA is a traditional monitor connector.

questions.question: State two examples of computer ports/connectors.
questions.answerText: USB port and VGA port.
questions.explanation: These are common connectors found on computers.

questions.question: Computer software is a collection of programs and related documentation.
questions.explanation: Software consists of programs, procedures and supporting files.

questions.question: Define computer software.
questions.answerText: Computer software is a collection of programs and instructions that direct a computer to perform specific tasks.
questions.explanation: Software enables hardware to function effectively.

questions.question: Software is generally classified into ______ and ______.
questions.explanation: Software is mainly divided into system and application software.

questions.question: Define system software.
questions.answerText: System software consists of programs that manage computer resources and provide a platform for application software.
questions.explanation: Examples include operating systems and utility programs.

questions.question: Which of the following is system software?
questions.explanation: Windows is an operating system.

questions.question: An operating system acts as an interface between the user and the computer hardware.
questions.explanation: The operating system manages communication between users and hardware.

questions.question: State four functions of an operating system.
questions.answerText: Memory management, file management, device management and process management.
questions.explanation: These are core operating system functions.

questions.question: Which function of an operating system controls computer memory?
questions.explanation: Memory management allocates and controls memory usage.

questions.question: Which operating system is commonly used on personal computers?
questions.explanation: All are examples of operating systems.

questions.question: Classify operating systems with examples.
questions.answerText: Single-user (Windows), Multi-user (UNIX), Real-time (RTOS), Distributed OS.
questions.explanation: Operating systems are classified based on functionality.

questions.question: A language translator converts source code into machine language.
questions.explanation: Translators enable computers to understand programs.

questions.question: Mention three examples of language translators.
questions.answerText: Compiler, Interpreter and Assembler.
questions.explanation: These are the main types of translators.

questions.question: Which translator converts assembly language into machine language?
questions.explanation: Assemblers translate assembly language.

questions.question: Utility programs are designed to maintain and optimize computer performance.
questions.explanation: Utilities help improve system efficiency.

questions.question: Define utility program.
questions.answerText: A utility program is system software designed to maintain, manage and optimize computer resources.
questions.explanation: Examples include antivirus and disk cleanup software.

questions.question: Which of the following is a utility program?
questions.explanation: All are examples of utility software.

questions.question: A device driver enables communication between hardware and the operating system.
questions.explanation: Drivers help the operating system control hardware devices.

questions.question: Define device driver.
questions.answerText: A device driver is software that enables communication between the operating system and a hardware device.
questions.explanation: Without drivers, hardware may not function properly.

questions.question: Which of the following requires a device driver?
questions.explanation: Most hardware devices require drivers.

questions.question: Application software is designed to perform specific user tasks.
questions.explanation: Application software helps users accomplish specific tasks.

questions.question: Define application software.
questions.answerText: Application software consists of programs designed to perform specific tasks for users.
questions.explanation: Examples include word processors and spreadsheets.

questions.question: Which of the following is application software?
questions.explanation: Microsoft Word is application software.

questions.question: Give three examples of application software.
questions.answerText: Microsoft Word, Microsoft Excel and PowerPoint.
questions.explanation: These are commonly used application packages.

questions.question: Customized application software is developed for a specific organization.
questions.explanation: Customized software is tailored to user requirements.

questions.question: State two advantages of customized application software.
questions.answerText: Meets specific user needs and provides better efficiency.
questions.explanation: Customized software is tailored to requirements.

questions.question: Which of the following is a disadvantage of customized software?
questions.explanation: Customized software is often expensive and time-consuming.

questions.question: Commercial application software is also known as ______ software.
questions.explanation: Commercial software is developed for mass use.

questions.question: State two advantages of commercial application software.
questions.answerText: Lower cost and immediate availability.
questions.explanation: Commercial software is readily available to users.

questions.question: Mention two guidelines for acquiring application software.
questions.answerText: Identify user requirements and consider software cost.
questions.explanation: Software selection should meet organizational needs.

questions.question: Arrange the generations of programming languages in order.
questions.answerText: 1GL, 2GL, 3GL, 4GL, 5GL.
questions.explanation: Programming languages evolved from machine language to AI-oriented languages.

questions.question: Data processing is the conversion of raw data into meaningful information.
questions.explanation: Data processing transforms raw facts into useful information.

questions.question: Define data processing.
questions.answerText: Data processing is the process of collecting, manipulating and transforming raw data into meaningful information.
questions.explanation: It helps organizations make informed decisions.

questions.question: Which of the following is the output of data processing?
questions.explanation: Processed data becomes information.

questions.question: Interactive processing allows direct communication between the user and computer.
questions.explanation: Users receive immediate responses from the system.

questions.question: Define interactive processing.
questions.answerText: Interactive processing is a mode where users communicate directly with the computer and receive immediate feedback.
questions.explanation: Examples include ATM transactions and online forms.

questions.question: Online processing involves processing data while connected to a computer system.
questions.explanation: Data is processed through a connected system.

questions.question: Define online processing.
questions.answerText: Online processing is a method where data is entered directly into a computer system and processed immediately.
questions.explanation: Common in banking and e-commerce systems.

questions.question: Transaction processing is commonly used in ______.
questions.explanation: Transaction processing records and processes business transactions.

questions.question: Define transaction processing.
questions.answerText: Transaction processing is the processing of business transactions such as sales, deposits and withdrawals.
questions.explanation: It ensures accurate and reliable transaction records.

questions.question: Real-time processing produces results immediately after data input.
questions.explanation: Real-time systems respond instantly.

questions.question: Give one example of a real-time processing system.
questions.answerText: Air traffic control system.
questions.explanation: Real-time systems require immediate responses.

questions.question: Batch processing handles data in groups called batches.
questions.explanation: Data is collected before processing.

questions.question: Which processing mode is commonly used for payroll preparation?
questions.explanation: Payroll data is usually processed periodically in batches.

questions.question: Define batch processing.
questions.answerText: Batch processing is a method where data is accumulated and processed together at a later time.
questions.explanation: It is suitable for repetitive tasks.

questions.question: Distributed processing involves multiple computers working together.
questions.explanation: Processing tasks are shared among different computers.

questions.question: Define distributed processing.
questions.answerText: Distributed processing is a method where processing tasks are shared among multiple computers connected through a network.
questions.explanation: It improves efficiency and reliability.

questions.question: Time-sharing processing allows multiple users to use a computer system simultaneously.
questions.explanation: CPU time is shared among users.

questions.question: Define time-sharing processing.
questions.answerText: Time-sharing processing is a system where many users share computer resources through time allocation.
questions.explanation: Each user receives a portion of CPU time.

questions.question: Multiprogramming involves executing several programs in memory at the same time.
questions.explanation: It improves CPU utilization.

questions.question: Define multiprogramming.
questions.answerText: Multiprogramming is the technique of keeping multiple programs in memory and executing them alternately.
questions.explanation: This minimizes CPU idle time.

questions.question: Multiprocessing involves the use of ______.
questions.explanation: Multiprocessing uses multiple processors simultaneously.

questions.question: Define multiprocessing.
questions.answerText: Multiprocessing is the use of two or more processors to execute tasks simultaneously.
questions.explanation: It increases processing speed.

questions.question: Offline processing occurs when data is processed without direct connection to the main computer.
questions.explanation: Data may be prepared before entering the main system.

questions.question: Define offline processing.
questions.answerText: Offline processing is a method where data is prepared and processed separately before being transferred to the main computer.
questions.explanation: It reduces the workload on the main system.

questions.question: Centralized processing means all processing activities are performed at a central location.
questions.explanation: A central computer handles all processing.

questions.question: Define centralized processing.
questions.answerText: Centralized processing is a system where all data processing activities are carried out by a central computer.
questions.explanation: Users depend on the central system.

questions.question: Decentralized processing distributes processing responsibilities among different locations.
questions.explanation: Different departments can process their own data.

questions.question: Define decentralized processing.
questions.answerText: Decentralized processing is a system where processing activities are performed by separate computers at different locations.
questions.explanation: It reduces dependence on a central computer.

questions.question: Which of the following is a criterion for choosing a data processing mode?
questions.explanation: Several factors influence the choice of processing mode.

questions.question: State five criteria for choosing a data processing mode.
questions.answerText: Cost, speed, accuracy, reliability and volume of data.
questions.explanation: Organizations consider these factors when selecting a processing method.
